findings.rationale: The proof is a nested interval construction whose key choices are spatial: each interval is trisected, T chooses the first closed third avoiding the enumerated value f(n), and recursion produces nested [a_n,b_n] whose supremum x lies in every retained interval but differs from every f(n). A compact interval diagram could clarify the three-way subdivision and nesting while the proof remains independent of it. This is a substantive candidate for a diagram, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.trisection: T(u,v,y) selects the first among [u,s], [s,t], [t,v] that omits y, where s=u+(v-u)/3 and t=s+(v-u)/3.
concrete_maps_and_relations.recursive_nesting: [a_{n+1},b_{n+1}] is one of the three closed thirds of [a_n,b_n] and omits f(n).
concrete_maps_and_relations.limit_point: x=sup{a_n} belongs to every [a_n,b_n], hence to (a,b), and x != f(n) for each n.

findings.rationale: The fact row renders the generated wikilink as literal Markdown text `[The power series ...](/library/item/...)` instead of a linked title. This is visible in the full-resolution tile and local HTML, while surrounding wikilinks in other items render as anchors. The source wikilink is valid; this is a local HTML rendering defect.
findings.concrete_content: The source link [[thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series]] in [L1] should display as a clickable title, but the captured ItemBody exposes its generated `[title](/library/item/id)` Markdown syntax.

findings.rationale: This is an explicitly planar vector-confinement example comparing two orderings of six unit vectors: the identity ordering stays within the claimed radius bound, while another ordering has a third partial sum outside it. A 2D vector/path diagram could make the two polygonal trajectories and the failed bound immediately visible. This is an editorial diagram candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.vectors: v=(e0,-e1,u,-e0,e1,-u), with e0=(1,0), e1=(0,1), u=(a,a), a=1/sqrt(2); six vectors have norm 1 and sum 0.
concrete_maps_and_relations.good_order: For identity order, partial sums s0,...,s6 are given at source line 52; their norms are at most 2.
concrete_maps_and_relations.bad_order: For order (e0,e1,u,-e0,-e1,-u), the third partial sum is (1+a,1+a), with norm greater than 2.
concrete_maps_and_relations.construction_auxiliary: The coefficient vector mu=(1,1/2,0,1,1/2,0) lies in Lambda={mu in [0,1]^6: sum mu_j v_j=0, sum mu_j=3}; dropping coordinate 5 gives the next admissible pair.

findings.rationale: The example is a geometric construction of the Möbius band from two parameter rectangles and two overlap components. The central result is that one overlap has matching induced normals while the overlap related by a 2π shift and s↦-s has opposite normals. A schematic of the band, patch rectangles, overlap components, and normal signs would make the main comparison much easier to see. This is an editorial diagram candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.surface_map: Psi(t,s)=((1+s cos(t/2))cos t,(1+s cos(t/2))sin t,s sin(t/2)).
concrete_maps_and_relations.patches: R1=[-pi/6,7pi/6]x[-1/2,1/2], R2=[5pi/6,13pi/6]x[-1/2,1/2]; each has angle width 4pi/3 and together covers a full turn.
concrete_maps_and_relations.first_overlap: K1=[5pi/6,7pi/6]x[-1/2,1/2]; both patches use identical parameters, so induced normals agree (at (pi,0), -e_x).
concrete_maps_and_relations.second_overlap: K2=[-pi/6,pi/6]x[-1/2,1/2] on R1 matches h(K2) on R2, h(t,s)=(t+2pi,-s); oriented area vectors reverse, e.g. at (0,0) -e_z vs +e_z.
